candidates.name: airbnb-sentiment-pricing

candidates.why_useful: Larger Vienna review corpus (320k) than a typical single Inside Airbnb pull; Vienna is not in our current 13-city/123-market panels, so this is incremental city coverage if the underlying review file is committed rather than fetched live.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: adds Vienna, a city not in our current stated panel

notes: This theme is a near-total dead end on GitHub as a place to find NEW data. Across ten dedicated European tourist-city searches (Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Copenhagen, Florence, Venice, Athens; Prague/Dublin/Lisbon returned empty or rate-limited before a usable result appeared) the results are overwhelmingly single-author student/portfolio EDA and price-prediction notebooks built on ONE current Inside Airbnb snapshot per city, exactly the pattern CONTEXT.md says to exclude for NYC-2019 — it generalizes to every one of these ten cities. No STR regulation trackers (Amsterdam vergunning/toeristische verhuur, Berlin Zweckentfremdung/Meldepflicht, Vienna, Lisbon RNAL, Dublin/Ireland short-term-let register), no municipal registry mirrors, no city-report data appendices, and no historical pre-2023 archived dumps turned up under any query tried (all returned empty, not just low-value). The two possibly-live leads (Data-Spaces-project's 2018 Berlin snapshot, which would hit gap #1 if the CSV is actually committed rather than pulled at runtime; and the 320k/635k-review Berlin/Vienna repos, which may hold larger stored review corpora than a bare listings snapshot) were NOT verified with a contents-listing call because both the gh search-API budget (repeatedly hit 403 rate-limit despite a nominal 6-call allowance — the shared 30/min limit was clearly being exhausted by other concurrent scouts) and the session's WebSearch budget (200/200 used before this scout could run a single query) were exhausted. A follow-up scout with fresh API budget should: (a) run `gh api repos/Data-Spaces-project/Berlin-Airbnb-Dataset-Analysis/contents` to check whether the 2018 Berlin CSV is actually committed, which would be a genuine gap-1 hit; (b) try Wayback Machine / direct site search instead of gh/WebSearch for the regulatory-registry side of this theme (Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Lisbon, Dublin all publish open STR/short-let registers on municipal open-data portals, but none of the searches found a GitHub mirror or client for them — that absence is itself worth recording, not just a null result from congestion); (c) note for whoever runs the next sweep: the gh search API rate limit is being shared/exhausted across concurrently-running scouts faster than the 30/min headline suggests — spacing out scout launches or serializing gh calls across the fleet would raise everyone's yield.
